newsitem.title: USA: U.S. will not get involved in Cargill/N Korea deal.
newsitem.headline: U.S. will not get involved in Cargill/N Korea deal.

text.p: The United States is not going to get involved in a grain deal being negotiated between Cargill Inc and North Korea, State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said Tuesday.

In response to a reporter's questions at the department's daily press briefing, Burns said, "I think the North Koreans are looking for a more active role by the United States government in these negotiations, but frankly we're not going to get involved. We don't get involved in commercial transactions."
A Cargill spokesperson told Reuters earlier Tuesday that the company views the transaction as strictly commercial, and that it has not asked the U.S. government to help in the financing.
Asked if the U.S. government could order Cargill to give North Korea the grain, Burn said, "No it cannot."

Cargill was approved last month to sell famine-struck North Korea 500,000 tonnes of wheat and/or rice. Cargill officials have been trying to work out the deal with North Korea since then, but the issue appears to have become embroiled in proposed diplomatic talks between the U.S. government and North Korea.
North Korean officials have delayed the talks twice and have said they wanted the grain deal with Cargill to be worked out first, before the talks take place.
